note: Independent baseline-scope rejudgment against RFC 4271 Section 5.1.2 in its propagation context: "When a given BGP speaker advertises the route to an internal peer, the advertising speaker SHALL NOT modify the AS_PATH attribute associated with the route." The assessed configuration is ordinary internal/external forwarding with the protocol AS_PATH behavior, including the existing migration-aware internal classification; explicitly selected operator extensions retain their own declared configuration and are not presented as default RFC behavior. General-forward tests assert the received path byte for byte toward internal recipients and useful local-AS prepend toward an external recipient. The new native route-server tests reach recordingConn-backed Session writers and independently assert exact internal/migration paths plus useful external protocol output. Their ordinary protocol-prepend case covers the default AS_PATH decision; configured as-override and typed export-edit cases add bounded extension-contract coverage. Source reads confirm both forwarding producers take the actual peer-derived internal verdict, run the export chain with that verdict and gate protocol prepend/override on isEBGP. Existing builder, export-chain and dry-run controls agree with the same classification. The old empty-path origination controls are supplementary construction witnesses and are not used as proof of learned-route preservation. The previously identified native RS guard gap is closed by the new units and selective guard experiments. This is in-process Session-writer evidence, not TCP or foreign-peer acceptance. The optional stale-modifier handoff is not an additional default-path gap: without an explicitly selected AS_PATH modifier, runStaleChain/libraryASPathOps records no AS_PATH edit, while the builder receives the actual peer role and preserves internal paths. The untagged stale-sender matrix separately exercises that explicit extension contract and is not credited as ordinary propagated-route evidence. Its actual missing/forced IsIBGP experiments were read as eight internal failures with four external passes, and four external failures with eight internal passes, respectively. Existing announce-origin remove-private semantics remain supported and are not relabelled as a default RFC advertisement claim. The independent judgment supports enforced ONLY after the main thread accepts all four current-wording native positive/negative records for the two new RS units; pending records are not asserted complete here. No claim is made that the separate refresh pre-policy provenance or RFC 2918 work is closed.
upgrade_reason: The previous weak verdict named the untested native route-server AS_PATH gates; new tagged tests now cover both the policy-role and protocol-edit gates at real Session writers with distinct internal and external assertions. Re-reading the owner's baseline-versus-explicit-extension rule also corrects the later over-broad demand for optional stale modifier coverage as a baseline prerequisite. No baseline requirement is excluded, no existing operator feature is removed, and formal current-unit discrimination records remain a precondition of stamping this upgrade.
